title: Secrets handling: one reader, zero leaks

concept.heading: A secret is read in one place, typed so it cannot print, and scrubbed from every log line
paragraphs: Module 0 put the CRM key in .env. This lesson makes that the rule for everything: a Settings model is the only code that reads the environment, every secret is a SecretStr (its repr is asterisks, its JSON is asterisks), and no other module ever touches os.environ for a key. Rotation becomes one edit to .env and a restart, which is the whole procedure a client needs written down.

Reminders do not stop leaks; structure does. A logging.Filter on the root logger rewrites every record before any handler sees it, replacing each known secret value with [redacted]. Install it once at startup from settings.secret_values(), and a log line like 'calling CRM with key %s' can never carry the key into a file, a ticket, or a model prompt.

The check is the same one from Module 0, generalized: it captures all logging, logs the key on purpose through an unrelated logger, and fails if the plain value appears. It also renders the settings three ways and fails if any secret shows.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: Connection references and environment variables in a Power Platform solution, plus the DLP policy that keeps a connector from posting secrets to chat. Here the connection reference is Settings and the DLP policy is the filter.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: pydantic SecretStr, logging.Filter, record.args
pythonBlock.intro: A LogRecord's message is msg % args, computed late. The filter must redact after formatting, then clear args so nothing re-expands.
pythonBlock.code:
import logging
from pydantic import BaseModel, SecretStr

class Settings(BaseModel):
    crm_api_key: SecretStr

s = Settings(crm_api_key="abc123xyz")
repr(s)                             # crm_api_key=SecretStr('**********')
s.crm_api_key.get_secret_value()    # the only way to get the plain value

class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record):
        text = record.getMessage()               # msg % args, formatted now
        for secret in self.secrets:              # longest first
            text = text.replace(secret, "[redacted]")
        record.msg, record.args = text, None     # nothing left to expand
        return True                              # never drop the record

spec: Implement load_settings(dotenv_path=None) and Settings.secret_values() per the stub: every secret is a SecretStr; MCP_TOKENS is split so each token value is scrubbed on its own.

Implement RedactingFilter.filter and install_redaction: longest secret first, values shorter than 4 characters ignored, record.args cleared after formatting, attached to the logger and to its existing handlers.
Call install_redaction(settings.secret_values()) at startup in mcp_server/server.py (both transports) so every server process is covered.
Write the rotation procedure as a three-line docstring at the top of settings.py: where the value lives, how to change it, what to restart.
askClaudeFor: The difference between a filter on a logger and a filter on a handler, and why install_redaction attaches to both.
A review of secret_values(): is there any secret the Settings holds that it does not return?
writeYourself: The filter body and the SecretStr fields.
The rotation procedure, in words a client can follow.

check.command: uv run --directory middleware python checks/run.py m3-1-secrets
check.summary: Settings load from the environment with SecretStr fields that never render; a missing CRM_API_KEY is a clear error; the filter redacts messages and args; captured logs from any logger contain [redacted] and never the key or a token.
